Title: Diagnosis of test `testStop3` failure in `PosixParserTest`

1. The test `testStop3` prepares an array of arguments `args` with elements `--zop==1`, `-abtoast`, and `--b=bar`.
2. The test then calls `parser.parse(options, args, true)` where the last argument `true` likely corresponds to the `stopAtNonOption` parameter which means the parser should stop parsing when a non-option argument is encountered.
3. The test expects `cl.getArgList().size()` to be 3, meaning all the input strings are recognized as extra arguments rather than options.
4. From the snippet of `Parser.parse(Options, String[], boolean)`:
   - It simply delegates to `parse(options, arguments, null, stopAtNonOption)` so the core parsing is happening in another overloaded method with a `Properties` argument.
   - This means the behavior depends heavily on the logic in the other `parse` method.
5. The failure likely occurred due to incorrect handling of the `stopAtNonOption` flag in the parsing method, possibly failing to stop parsing at the right position or incorrectly identifying options vs extra arguments.
6. This would result in `cl.getArgList()` having a size different from 3, either because it wrongly parsed some options or stopped too late/early.

To confirm, next steps:
- Examine the main parsing implementation, probably `Parser.parse(Options, String[], Properties, boolean)`.
- Investigate the logic concerning the `stopAtNonOption` flag and how the arguments list (`getArgList()`) is constructed.

I will now fetch the code for `Parser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], java.util.Properties, boolean)` to further diagnose the cause.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
